summary.en: Comparisons produce int zero or one.
summary.bn: ছয়টি comparison লিখে ০ বা ১ ফল বোঝো এবং দশমিকের তুলনায় tolerance বেছে নাও।

notes: The comparison result is int zero or one in C17, as in earlier editions. The numeric conversion rules still apply. A change of output format does not change those operand conversions or repair an unsuitable floating comparison.

examples.title: Check the passing boundary
examples.explanationHtml: Forty does not exceed forty, but it reaches the inclusive threshold and equals it. The results are zero, one and one. Looking at all three questions together makes the meaning of the equals bar visible at the passing boundary.

examples.title: Compare two scores
examples.explanationHtml: Theory is larger than lab, so the less-than test is false and the greater-than test is true. The values are also unequal. Each result is an int truth value rather than a copy of either score.

examples.title: Use a measurement tolerance
examples.explanationHtml: The permitted absolute error is one millionth in the chosen units. The difference between these small finite values is below that limit, so the result is one. The tolerance is written explicitly so a reader can judge whether it suits the measurement.

practice.title: At least forty
practice.statementHtml: Read marks 0 to 100. After the prompt Input: , print 1 for marks at least 40, otherwise 0, and newline.

practice.title: Different roll numbers
practice.statementHtml: Read a and b, each 0 to 9999. After the prompt Input: , print 1 if different, otherwise 0, and newline.

practice.title: A valid closed range
practice.statementHtml: Read x from -100 to 100. After the prompt Input: , print 1 when x is from 10 to 20 inclusive, otherwise 0; end with newline.

practice.title: Nearest hundredth
practice.statementHtml: Read two finite doubles from -1000 to 1000. After the prompt Input: , print 1 when their absolute difference is at most 0.01, otherwise 0; end the line.
hints: Compare a nonnegative difference with the stated tolerance.

quiz.prompt: What type does a C relational expression produce?
quiz.explanation: Its value is zero or one.

quiz.prompt: Which operator asks whether marks equals 40?
Which comparison includes the upper boundary 100?
quiz.explanation: Less than or equal includes equality.

quiz.prompt: How should a closed range be expressed in C?
quiz.explanation: Each comparison is complete and AND requires both.

quiz.prompt: Why may 0.1 + 0.2 fail an exact equality check with 0.3?
options: Binary floating arithmetic can approximate the values
quiz.explanation: A small representation difference may remain.

quiz.prompt: Who determines a useful comparison tolerance?
options: The task units and error requirement
quiz.explanation: A tolerance suitable for one measurement can be unsuitable for another.

quiz.prompt: Does a comparison modify its operands?
quiz.explanation: Ordinary comparisons compute a result without assignment.

quiz.prompt: At the passing threshold, which two truth values are produced?
quiz.explanation: Only the inclusive test accepts forty.

quiz.prompt: Unequal scores are compared for equality. What is printed?
Which result comes from testing negative three against zero?
quiz.explanation: Negative three is less than zero, giving one.

keyPoints.en: Comparisons produce int zero or one.
A chained inequality needs two tests and logical AND.
keyPoints.bn: দুই সীমার মাঝে আছে কি না দেখতে দুই test-কে && দিয়ে জুড়ো।
দশমিক তুলনার tolerance কাজের প্রয়োজন অনুযায়ী ঠিক করো।

examQuestions.question: What type does a C relational expression produce?
examQuestions.answerHtml: int. Its value is zero or one.

examQuestions.question: Which operator asks whether marks equals 40?

examQuestions.answerHtml:
0 1

Only the inclusive test accepts forty.

examQuestions.question: Read two finite doubles from -1000 to 1000. After Input: print 1 when their absolute difference is at most 0.01, otherwise 0; end the line.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void)
{
    double a, b;
    printf("Input: ");
    if (scanf("%lf %lf", &a, &b) != 2 || a < -1000 || a > 1000
        || b < -1000 || b > 1000) {
        return 1;
    }
    double difference = a - b;
    if (difference < 0) {
        difference = -difference;
    }
    printf("%d\n", difference <= 0.01);
    return 0;
}

Compare a nonnegative difference with the stated tolerance.
